title: Healthcare Inference Pilot Playbook and Security Guide
author: Sofia Patel
content:
Purpose
=======
This playbook is a go-to-market and engineering-aligned guide for running a successful inference pilot with regulated healthcare customers. It covers positioning and messaging, a concise competitive brief, archetypal pilot scope, security & compliance checkpoints (PHI/PII handling, BAA, encryption), pricing scenarios, a sample customer case study, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this document when engaging hospitals, digital health startups, or payer platforms considering production LLM inference.

Executive summary
-----------------
- Objective: Convert a 4–8 week pilot into a committed deployment (Dedicated or Private) by demonstrating safety, latency, cost predictability, and compliance controls.
- Key buyer personas: Platform/infra engineers, Head of ML, Security/Privacy Officer, Health IT/Integrations, Procurement.
- Success metrics for pilot: PHI-safe API surface, latency P99 < 350ms (for text assistant workflows), end-to-end accuracy parity within ±2% vs baseline, controlled inference unit cost <= target.

Positioning and messaging (one-liners)
-------------------------------------
- For security and compliance leads: "Run regulated LLM inference with a vendor that provides a private control plane, BAA-ready tooling, KMS integrations, and audit-grade logging—without rebuilding your serving stack."
- For platform/ML engineers: "Ship predictable, low-latency inference across hosted, dedicated, and VPC/private deployments with the same API, rollout tooling, and observability."
- For product owners: "Deliver a safer, faster clinical assistant with model-level rollouts and behavioral regression alerts to keep production quality steady as models evolve."

Quick competitive brief
-----------------------
- Primary competitors considered by healthcare buyers: large cloud vendor-managed endpoints, specialized inference service vendors, and open-source self-hosted stacks.
- Redwood differentiation: Unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, turnkey BAA-ready controls, KV/prefix caching to reduce PHI surface and cost, deterministic rollouts + eval hooks for quality regressions.
- Seller bullets vs typical objections:
  - "We already have model endpoints in the cloud": Redwood supports VPC Private deployments + audit logs + KMS to match security posture while offering lower per-token cost through runtime optimizations.
  - "We need on-prem": Use Redwood Private (on-prem packaging + air-gapped install) with documented day-2 ops and upgrade paths.
  - "We worry about hallucinations and regressions": Redwood Optimize integrates evals and regression alerts tied to your canonical prompt set and clinical prompts.

Pilot scope: recommended configuration
------------------------------------
- Duration: 4–8 weeks (negotiable).
- Workloads: clinical summarization, triage-assist prompts, discharge note templates (avoid direct diagnostic replacement during pilot).
- Deployment options: start with VPC Private or Dedicated in the region the customer requires. Hosted may be acceptable for non-PHI-sandboxed pilots.
- Models: include one production-calibrated LLM (quantized variant) + a smaller fallback model for degraded mode.
- SLOs and targets:
  - Latency: P95 < 200ms, P99 < 350ms for typical 512-token requests.
  - Availability: 99.9% (pilot-focused).
  - Cost targets: aim to show >=25% improvement from customer baseline via caching/quantization.

Pilot timeline and responsibilities (numbered)
--------------------------------------------
1. Pre-sales checklist (week -1 to 0): legal (BAA draft), security Ask (networking, IP allowlist), initial data sample request, define pilot success criteria. Owner: AE + SE.
2. Kickoff (day 0): architecture review, data flows, roles/contacts, and rollback plan. Owner: Solutions Engineer.
3. Deployment (days 1–7): Provision Dedicated or Private environment, integrate KMS, configure audit logging. Owner: Infra Eng + Customer IT.
4. Integration & prompts (days 7–14): run prompt calibration, add prefix/KV caching policies, measure throughput. Owner: ML Eng + Customer ML.
5. Evaluation (days 14–28): run structured evals, compare quality metrics, run security tests (pen-test checklist). Owner: Applied ML + Security.
6. Review & conversion (days 28–42): present results, propose committed capacity and price. Owner: AE + Product Specialist.

Technical configuration examples
--------------------------------
YAML example for Dedicated node config (pilot-sized):

service: redwood-dedicated
region: us-east-1
instance_type: a100-40gb
replicas: 2
model_pinning: |
  - model_name: redwood-clinical-v1-q4
    max_seq_len: 2048
    quantization_profile: q4_0
    fallback_policy: small-llm

Observability & SLOs (table)
----------------------------
| Metric | Pilot Target | Owner | Alert threshold |
|--------|--------------|-------|-----------------|
| Request latency (P95) | <200ms | Platform | >250ms for 5m |
| Error rate (4xx/5xx) | <1% | Oncall | >2% for 10m |
| Tokens per second | Baseline+20% | Capacity | Sustained >80% of limit |
| Quality regression (eval score) | <=1.5% drop | Applied ML | >2% drop |

Pricing guidance (example scenarios)
-----------------------------------
- Hosted pilot (no PHI): metered usage, typical pilot spend $5k–$20k depending on traffic and eval runs. Per-token example: $0.0006 per 1k prompt tokens (example).
- Dedicated pilot (recommended for PHI): reserved monthly seat + metered overage. Example pilot pricing: $18,000/month reserved for 2x A100-equivalent nodes (pilot discount applied) + usage egress fees.
- Conversion proposal: tiered committed capacity with volume discounts; include migration credits for pilot artifacts and sustained discount for 12m commit.

Sales collateral: prospect talking points and objection handling
------------------------------------------------------------
- Trusted controls: "We provide an auditable control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and a documented BAA offering to minimize legal friction."
- Speed to production: "Same API and SDKs across deployment models — your integration work is reusable when you move from pilot to Dedicated or Private."
- TCO framing: Present cost delta from customer baseline and show runtime levers (batching, caching, quantization) that yield unit cost reductions.

Case study: MediTrack Health (pilot summary)
------------------------------------------
- Customer: MediTrack Health (fictional but representative midsize telehealth provider).
- Pilot duration: 6 weeks.
- Scope: discharge-summary drafting and triage-assist workflows (non-diagnostic).
- Outcome:
  - Latency: P95 improved from 320ms (baseline) to 180ms.
  - Cost: unit token cost reduced by 38% after enabling prefix caching and a q4 quantized model.
  - Quality: clinical summary ROUGE-L maintained within 0.8% of baseline.
  - Business result: product team moved to a 12-month Dedicated commitment with a projected 3x throughput target.

Security & compliance checklist (must-complete before pilot with PHI)
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Signed BAA in place.
- VPC / private connectivity or on-prem deployment approved.
- KMS/HSM integration for keys; customer controls encryption keys where required.
- Audit logs enabled for all inference requests and model activities; retention agreed.
- Data minimization applied to prompts: strip direct PHI where possible; map identifiers rather than free-text.
- Penetration test schedule and responsible parties documented.

Prospect-facing Security FAQ (concise)
------------------------------------
Q: Do you sign a BAA?
A: Yes. Redwood has a standard BAA template and a track record of signing BAAs with healthcare customers. For on-prem or air-gapped installs, the BAA is scoped to the delivered package and support model.

Q: How is PHI protected in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
A: Hosted: recommended only for non-PHI pilots. Dedicated: physically isolated compute and tenant separation; network controls and audit logs. Private: full control plane in your VPC or on-premises with keys and logs under your management. All modes support KMS/HSM.

Q: Can you restrict model access and keep raw prompts out of logs?
A: Yes. We support redaction and selective logging (masking policies) and can route logging for sensitive endpoints to a customer-managed SIEM.

Q: What certifications do you maintain?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for our hosted control plane and provides documentation packages for customer security review. For Private deployments, we provide hardened packaging and guidance to satisfy certs under customer responsibility.

Q: What is your data retention and deletion policy for pilot artifacts?
A: Pilot artifacts retention is configurable; short pilot default is 30 days unless customer requests otherwise. Deletion requests for customer-provided artifacts are honored and logged.

Conversion & next steps checklist for AE/SEs
-------------------------------------------
- Package: pilot report (metrics + logs + evals), proposed Dedicated config, proposed committed pricing and SLA.
- Internal approvals required: Legal (BAA + contract terms), Security (final acceptance), Solutions Architecture (resource sizing).
- Conversion play: schedule executive review, prepare migration runbook (reuse prompts and caches), and offer a 4–8 week discount window for earlier conversion.

-------------------------
